problems.label: Highs and lows that disrupt life and safety
definitions: Has had at least one period of days with much less sleep, racing ideas, big plans or spending, and actions that caused serious problems at home, work or with money.
Has periods of low mood, low energy and withdrawal that take up weeks.
Sleep and daily routine shift sharply before or during episodes.
longTermGoals: Fewer and shorter mood episodes, caught early, with a steady routine and a plan the client and family trust.

shortTermObjectives.text: Within 2 weeks, attend a psychiatric evaluation and bring a written list of questions about medication benefits and side effects.
By session 4, describe in own words at least 3 personal early warning signs of a high and 3 of a low.
For 4 weeks, log daily wake time, bedtime, first contact and main meal with a mood rating, and keep wake time within 1 hour of the target on at least 5 days a week.
By session 6, complete a staying-well plan with early signs, first steps and contacts, and share it with one trusted person if the client chooses.
By session 2, complete a written safety plan with warning signs, coping steps, people and services to contact, and steps to make the home safer, and review it at least monthly.
Complete the PHQ-9 at intake and every 2 to 4 weeks; if a high or a low lasts more than a few days, contact the prescriber within 48 hours.

collaborativeNote: Write goals and objectives with the client in their own words. Timelines and targets are examples to adapt; the client decides what matters, and the clinician checks safety and fit.
